meta.name: seo-blog-pipeline
meta.author: Mahesh Revenueholic
meta.description: Full SEO blog pipeline. Auto-installs skills, runs 5-phase workflow, delivers publish-ready content.

flow: 2. Scrape GitHub repo for all files + raw content
3. Diff local vs remote: NEW, CHANGED, UNCHANGED, LOCAL_ONLY
4. Install only NEW and CHANGED. Skip UNCHANGED. Don't touch LOCAL_ONLY.
rules: Check local first before scraping GitHub
Compare content, not just existence
Install every skill, but only if new or changed
Never delete local files not on GitHub
No external dependencies, only the public GitHub repo

inputs.optional_auto: All optional fields (secondary keywords, search intent, audience, word count, tone, competitor URLs, internal links, CTAs, data, FAQ, TOC, meta title/description) are AUTO-resolved by the agent via SERP analysis, client website scraping, and web research.

guardrail: Do not proceed if client, client_website, primary_keyword, or b2b_or_b2c is null or empty.
workflow: PHASE 1: CONTEXT → PHASE 2: SERP → PHASE 3: MCQ → PHASE 4: WRITE→REVIEW→POLISH → PHASE 5: DELIVER

steps: 1. Check memory and saved context for brand voice, prior posts, topic preferences
2. Check installed skills. Match against seo-blog-b2b/b2c, fuck-slop, competitor-page-assessor, human-write
3. Scrape client website homepage + blog. Extract: brand voice, content topics, feature page URLs, CTA patterns
4. Record what you know. Don't ask about anything you already have
5. Begin AUTO research for optional fields resolvable from client website
phase_1_context.quality_gate: All sources checked. Brand voice detected or requested. AUTO fields partially resolved.

steps: 1. Search primary keyword. Identify top 5 ranking pages
2. Scrape each. Assess using competitor-page-assessor skill (or: format, clarity, depth, unique angle, word count, internal linking)
3. Identify SERP gaps: missing angles, underserved audiences, absent formats
4. Choose differentiation format (if all listicles → write guide; if all guides → write opinionated comparison)
5. Resolve AUTO fields: search_intent, content_format, target_word_count, secondary_keywords
phase_2_serp.quality_gate: Top 5 assessed. Gaps identified. Differentiation angle defined. AUTO fields resolved.

rules: Don't ask about anything found in Phase 1 or 2
Round 1: ALL foundational MCQs in one message (topic/angle, audience, goal, length, tone, key points, data, CTA)
Round 2+: Advanced MCQs for nuanced points (controversial takes, examples, brand-sensitive topics, internal links)
Each MCQ: 3-5 specific options + 'Other (please specify)'
Move to writing once you have enough. Don't over-question
HARD GATE: Must present MCQs and receive answers before Phase 4. Do not skip. Do not auto-answer.
Only proceed if 100% confident in the topic
phase_3_mcq.quality_gate: All foundational questions answered. Agent 100% confident. No ambiguity.

phase_4_three_agent.description: Three distinct passes. Do not compress.

writer.task: Write first draft using seo-blog-b2b or seo-blog-b2c skill (line by line, don't skim)
rules: Follow brand writing style from context/memory/website
Apply at least 3 engagement techniques
Research every tool/vendor via web search before writing. Cite sources.
Structure: clear headings, 1-3 sentence paragraphs, scannable
Each tool gets its own H3. No comparison tables as substitute.
Every H2 contains a keyword or variation
Vary section structure. Repetitive structure is an AI tell.
Target: 2000-3500 words. Minimum 1500.
If include_faq=true: 4-6 FAQ questions from PAA data. FAQ schema.
Grade 5 reading level. Short sentences. Plain words.
Third person. No 'I/we/our' except: direct quotes, About section, or establishing source of insight.
Don't announce actions. Execute them.
writer.quality_gate: Draft complete. Tools verified. Paragraphs 1-3 sentences. H2s have keywords. Each tool has H3. No banned patterns. Word count met. 3+ engagement techniques. Third person.

reviewer.task: Run fuck-slop skill in a LOOP until clean. Minimum 5 runs. Check if installed first — if not, install from GitHub.
rules: Run every banned pattern check against FULL draft, not sample
LITERAL MATCH: Search for 'Most guides', 'Every listicle', 'If you search for', 'Most resources', 'Most articles', 'If you look at'. Flag as Critical if found.
Review: clarity, specificity, brand voice, factual accuracy, structure, CTA, SEO basics, paragraph length, H2 keywords, structural variation, reading level

ENGAGEMENT CHECK: Named frameworks? Specific numbers? Blunt skips? Surprising opening? Threaded narrative? Sticky closing? Tradeoffs as implications? Varied tool sections? Rate each Strong/Needs Work/Weak.
If compliant but flat: flag Critical — 'Draft passes checks but fails engagement. Apply techniques in Polisher.'
Rate each criterion Strong/Needs Work/Weak with specific evidence (quote the line)
Prioritized fix list (Critical to Nice-to-have)
Rewrite the draft
Check every tool/vendor claim against source. Unverifiable = Critical.
Check for repetitive patterns: same closing phrase, same sentence structure, same paragraph shape
Check third-person compliance
reviewer.quality_gate: Every line reviewed. Every banned pattern checked via literal match. Every tool claim verified. Engagement assessed. Prioritized fix list complete with evidence.

polisher.task: Final draft based on reviewer's feedback
rules: Address every Critical and Needs Work item
Maintain writer's voice and structure
ENGAGEMENT PASS: If flagged as flat, rewrite using engagement techniques. Minimum 3 applied.
Write title tag (50-60 chars, keyword near front), meta description (155-160 chars, keyword + CTA hook), URL slug
Brief Editor's Note at top: what changed from draft to final
Re-run banned pattern detection. Fix any remaining.
Re-run engagement check. Rewrite until 3+ techniques present.
Verify grade 5 reading level. Simplify complex sentences.
Verify all tool claims still sourced after editing
Verify FAQ present and quality if include_faq=true
Verify internal links included and correct
Verify third-person compliance
Don't announce. Execute.
polisher.quality_gate: All Critical/Needs Work addressed. Banned patterns clean. 3+ engagement techniques. Grade 5 verified. Claims sourced. FAQ present if required. Internal links included. Third person maintained. Title/meta/slug written.

output: 1. Final blog post (full, ready to publish)
6. Internal linking (auto-linked if scraped, suggested if not)
8. AUTO field report: which were researched vs. defaulted. Flag any for user verification.
phase_5_delivery.quality_gate: All items present. Word count met. Claims sourced. No banned patterns. Grade 5. Internal links included or noted. Editor's note present. 3+ engagement techniques. Third person.

core_rules.description: Fallback rules used if skills are not available. If skills ARE loaded, follow them as primary and use these as reinforcement only.
writing: Every H2: contains keyword or variation. Generic labels banned.
Each tool: own H3 section. No tables as substitute.
Reading level: grade 5. Short sentences. Plain words.
Vary section structure. Repetitive = AI tell.
Third person. First person only for: direct quotes, About section, establishing source of insight.
Every tool/vendor: verified via web search before writing. Cite source. No fabrication.
Complete tasks in one response. Don't end with 'I'll do X next' unless X is next user step.
banned_patterns: Confrontational opening ('Most guides...', 'Every listicle...', 'If you search for...')
Comparison tables instead of individual H3s
Repetitive closing patterns ('Where it fits:', 'The tradeoff is...')
Generic capability assessments ('strength is breadth', 'depth is moderate')
Self-announced honesty ('No tool is perfect', 'We call out tradeoffs')
Manufactured emphasis ('The key word is', 'What most people don't realize')
Buzzwords (leverage, streamline, synergy, robust, comprehensive, cutting-edge, best-in-class, purpose-built)
engagement_techniques: Name your frameworks (e.g., 'Death by launch-and-leave' not 'Common failure pattern #1')
Use specific numbers and thresholds (e.g., 'adoption drops when it takes 15+ seconds' not 'ease of use matters')
Be blunt in skip recommendations (e.g., 'Everyone else should skip it' not 'may not be suitable')
Open with something surprising (not 'there are many platforms on the market')
Thread one narrative through the whole piece (not disconnected sections)
End with a line that sticks (not 'Choose the right platform for your needs')
State tradeoffs as practical implications (e.g., '$3,000 minimum means 60+ users' not 'has a $3,000 minimum')
Vary tool section structure (different headers/structure for each tool)

guardrails: No fabrication of data, quotes, statistics, or case studies
Don't skip review stage. If no review skill, use core_rules.banned_patterns as checklist.
If steps exceed 30: deliver best available output with note
If blocked: self-diagnose (missing data → use AUTO or ask; missing capability → use fallback; ambiguity → use most reasonable interpretation + note). Continue. Don't stop and wait.
Don't announce actions without executing. Biggest time waster.
If skills not available: use core_rules as primary instruction set. Note in output.
If web search not available: use training data + disclaimer. Flag all tool claims for manual verification.
If brand voice not detected: use default (direct, practical, honest, no buzzwords, grade 5). Note in output.
Target: 10-15 minutes per blog. Zero revision rounds. Quality built in first pass.
Apply at least 3 engagement techniques. Compliant-but-boring = failed draft.
If content too similar to ranking pages: pivot to underserved angle. Don't produce slightly different version of what exists.
If conflicting instructions: flag to user. Use more specific instruction. If user specified explicitly, follow user. If AUTO, follow guardrail.
